h1: The 6 Best Microwave Toaster Oven Combos of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Microwave Oven Combos: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the best microwave and air fryer combo ovens for 2026, compared on wattage, price tier and countertop fit.
summary: The Toshiba countertop air fryer combo is the best microwave toaster oven combo here, a 1000W unit with air fry in the $200 to $500 tier. The OptiChef PRO MAX adds 100W at 1100W. The GE and Frigidaire are the cheaper options, but they leave wattage unstated.
intro: Anyone who wants a combo appliance discovers the label is vague. Some products blend a microwave with an air fryer, others with a convection oven or toaster oven, so reading the feature list matters more than the product name. A microwave that air fries is not a toaster oven, and a few listings blur the two on purpose.

We reviewed the listings for these combos and ranked them on wattage, listed cooking functions and price tier. Several listings give only a few specs, so we note where detail is thin. We left out an over-the-range microwave since it is not a countertop combo. Four of the six are Toshibas, which makes the stated differences small and the missing ones important.

products.name: TOSHIBA Countertop Microwave Oven Air Fryer Combo
products.verdict: A 1000W countertop microwave with air fry, from a brand that fills this niche.
products.description:
This Toshiba pairs 1000W of microwave power with an air fry function in one countertop unit, in the $200 to $500 tier. Combining the two modes saves a whole appliance's counter space, and the air fry mode crisps food that a microwave alone leaves soggy, such as leftover fries and breaded chicken.

It leads because it combines the two functions buyers look for in a combo with a clear wattage figure. The GE and Frigidaire list air fry but no wattage, which makes them harder to judge. The tradeoff against them is cost, since this model sits in the upper tier.

It suits a household that wants to replace a microwave and an air fryer with one appliance. The caveat is interior size: the listing gives little on it, so check dimensions against your counter and your largest dish.
products.idealFor: Households wanting one appliance to microwave and air fry.

products.name: TOSHIBA OptiChef PRO MAX Air Fryer Combo Microwave Oven
products.verdict: The most powerful microwave in this list at 1100W, with air fry.
products.description:
The OptiChef PRO MAX lists 1100W and an air fry function, in the $200 to $500 tier. Wattage is the speed of microwave heating, and 100W more shortens reheat times modestly. It carries a branded PRO MAX line name, but the listing gives few other specs.

It takes second place because its extra 100W over the 1000W Toshibas is the only hard spec advantage the listings offer. Beyond that, it is similar in function to the pick above and costs the same tier. A 10 percent power gain helps with dense foods more than with a mug of water.

Choose it if microwave power is your priority. The caveat is that wattage alone does not tell you about cooking evenness, so read the full listing for features and interior size.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the highest wattage in a microwave and air fryer combo.

products.name: TOSHIBA 4-in-1 Microwave Oven with Air Fryer Combo
products.description:
This Toshiba is sold as a 4-in-1 with 1000W of power and an air fry function, in the $200 to $500 tier. Four-in-one branding implies more cooking modes than a plain microwave, but the listing here does not name them, which leaves you to infer.

It is placed behind the first two since its listing adds the 4-in-1 label without spelling out the functions. The core specs, 1000W and air fry, match the top pick, so the label has to carry the extra value. It ties the Toshiba countertop on power and tier, and gives up 100W to the OptiChef.

It works for buyers drawn to multi-function branding. The caveat is the vague function list: read the listing to confirm exactly which four modes it offers before you pay.
products.skipIf: You want a clear function list.

products.name: TOSHIBA 4-in-1 Countertop Microwave Oven with Air Fryer
products.verdict: A near twin of the other 4-in-1, explicitly countertop, at 1000W.
products.description:
This is another 4-in-1 Toshiba, listed as countertop, with 1000W and air fry, in the $200 to $500 tier. Calling it countertop outright answers a question the other 4-in-1 leaves open, namely whether it needs built-in installation.

It trails the other 4-in-1 only because the two are so alike on paper that there is little to separate them. Pick whichever is easier to find. Against the first Toshiba, it adds the 4-in-1 label with the same wattage, so the decision is about features you cannot see in the data. The price tier is the same for all four Toshibas.

It suits shoppers who want the countertop label stated outright. The caveat is duplication: compare the two 4-in-1 listings carefully, because the differences, if any, are not in the specs.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a clearly labeled countertop 4-in-1.

products.name: GE GCST10A1WSS Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A GE countertop microwave listed with air fry, in the $100-200 tier.
products.description:
This GE countertop microwave lists an air fry function and sits in the $100 to $200 tier. A lower price puts air frying within reach of a smaller budget, and a known appliance brand adds a service network that unknown names lack.

It lands fifth because it gives no wattage in the listing data, unlike the Toshibas, though it costs a full tier less. You trade a stated power figure for a lower price. Without watts you cannot gauge heating speed, and the air fry detail is limited to the single word.

It makes sense for a smaller budget. The caveat is the missing wattage and size: confirm both on the listing before buying, since a weak microwave with air fry may disappoint.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting air fry on a countertop microwave.
products.skipIf: You want a stated wattage figure.

products.name: FRIGIDAIRE 1.2 cu ft Microwave
products.verdict: A 1.2 cu ft microwave with an air fry function at the lowest price tier here.
products.description:
This Frigidaire is a 1.2 cu ft microwave listed with air fry, in the $100 to $200 tier. It is the only pick that states interior capacity, and 1.2 cu ft is a mid size that holds a standard dinner plate on most turntables.

It is last because it offers the least detail among the picks, though that stated capacity helps judge whether it fits a family-size dish. It matches the GE on tier but gives a size where the GE gives nothing. The wattage is not shown, so heating speed is a guess.

It works for buyers who want to spend under $200. The caveat is wattage and the air fry details: check both on the listing, because a combo that crisps poorly defeats the purpose.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a combo under $200 with known capacity.
products.skipIf: You want a high stated wattage.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is microwave power, and higher numbers heat food faster. The picks here range from 1000W to 1100W where stated. Look for the wattage in the listing title or specs, and treat a missing figure as a flag. The GE and Frigidaire do not show it in our data, so heating time is a guess until you check the manufacturer page.

An air fry mode circulates hot air to crisp food, which a plain microwave cannot do. It is why these combos cost more. Check the listing names air fry as a function, and look for any accessory like a crisping tray or basket. Air fry on a combo is typically smaller than on a stand-alone air fryer.

Capacity in cubic feet determines which dishes fit. A 1.2 cu ft interior is a common mid size. Look for the cu ft figure and compare it with your largest plate. Only the Frigidaire states one in our data. Air fry also needs room for air to move, so a full cavity crisps less well.

A combo oven is bulky, and you need clearance for ventilation. Measure your counter and the space above and behind the unit first. Check the listed dimensions, since the Toshiba listings here do not state them in our data, and allow for the cord length and the door swing.

Tiers split into just two bands here, $100 to $200 and $200 to $500. More money buys a stated wattage and a clearer function list, not necessarily better cooking. Match the tier to how heavily you will use the air fry mode, and weigh it against buying a stand-alone air fryer, which often crisps more evenly.

faq.q: Is a microwave air fryer combo a toaster oven?
faq.a: Not exactly. Most listings here combine a microwave with air fry rather than a toaster oven. Read each listing for the cooking functions it names, then confirm whether it browns food, including any bake or convection mode, and any accessories in the box.

faq.q: What is a common mistake buying a combo?
faq.a: Assuming the name means the same functions everywhere. Check whether air fry is listed, and look for the wattage. The GE and Frigidaire omit it, while the Toshibas state 1000W or 1100W.

faq.q: Is the OptiChef PRO MAX worth it over the TOSHIBA Countertop?
faq.a: It offers 1100W against 1000W, in the same price tier. If power is your priority it is the better choice, but the other specs are similar, so the gain is modest and you should check the price.
Place it on a stable counter with clearance for ventilation. Follow the manual for the first use, and run an empty air fry cycle if it recommends one to burn off residue. Keep the vents clear.
Wipe the interior after use and clean any air fry accessories according to the manual. Grease buildup in a combo can smoke, so avoid letting it sit, and let the unit cool before wiping.

faq.q: Why was the over-the-range GE excluded?
faq.a: It is a built-in over-the-range microwave rather than a countertop combo, so it does not fit this list. Our focus is countertop units like the Toshiba and Frigidaire models, which sit on a counter without installation.

finalTake: Buy the Toshiba countertop air fryer combo for the clearest wattage and function listing. Choose the OptiChef PRO MAX if microwave speed is the priority, and the Frigidaire if you want a stated 1.2 cu ft interior under $200. Always confirm the cooking functions on the full listing, because the word combo covers several different machines.
